Optimization Insights & Recommendations

Synthesizing findings into concrete, actionable interventions for infrastructure managers and grid planners.

1. Load Shifting & Time-of-Use Pricing
Peak periods show elevated station loads and longer queues. Introduce time-of-use pricing incentives to shift discretionary charging to Off-Peak windows, where renewable ratios are also more favorable.

2. Queue Management at Highway Stations
Highway locations experience the highest waiting times and queue lengths, especially during Peak slots. Deploy dynamic queue alerts and consider additional fast-charger capacity at top-demand highway stations.

3. Renewable-Aligned Charging Incentives
Renewable energy ratios vary significantly by weather and time slot. Offer discounted rates during high-renewable windows (Clear weather + Off-Peak) to maximize green energy utilization and improve optimization rewards.

4. Station-Level Capacity Expansion
Top 15 stations by demand account for a disproportionate share of load. Prioritize infrastructure investment at these high-throughput nodes, with a focus on Urban and Highway corridors.

5. Vehicle-Type Aware Scheduling
Larger vehicles (Buses, Trucks) consume more energy and occupy chargers longer. Implement priority rules or dedicated high-power bays for heavy fleet vehicles to reduce overall system wait times.

6. Grid Stress Monitoring by Day & Slot
Weekday Peak slots show the highest station loads. Activate demand-response protocols and temporary power caps during these windows to prevent grid stress and negative optimization rewards.

Bottom Line: The network shows clear temporal and spatial stress patterns. A coordinated strategy—combining time-of-use pricing, queue management, renewable-aligned incentives, and targeted capacity expansion—will improve customer experience, grid stability, and sustainability outcomes.
